note:
Paper 81, Team 33900, a 2015 paper that models the human capital network of an imaginary company called ICM - 370 employees assigned to offices by a genetic algorithm, a personnel relationship graph, a directed organisational graph, AHP scoring of turnover intention, and then a two-year simulation of churn, promotion, recruitment and productivity. Twenty pages, thirteen measured regions on ten pages: twelve exhibit rows and one excluded fragment. The paper numbers eleven figures and four tables.

What the exhibits are. Three structural diagrams (the org chart, the AHP hierarchy and the multiplex picture), two node-link graphs of the same company at two different resolutions (personnel relationship and organisational), one two-panel scatter of turnover intention at month 6 against month 8, two stacked-bar records of monthly productivity, and three line charts of the simulation - turnover intention against average productivity on a dual axis, the two cost curves on another dual axis, and worker count under three churn rates. The symbol table is the only grid with a measured region.

The finding worth carrying out of this paper is Table 4. It prints the same twelve numbers as Table 3 - 2.314, 2.083, 2.250 for the promoted count, 0.378, 0.353, 0.374 for productivity, 3.378, 3.372, 3.741 for senior-manager productivity, 35.16, 38.33, 37.00 for middle-manager count - under a caption that promises a different parameter sweep, and the prose then reads the second as independent confirmation of the first. Neither grid has a measured region, so both are declared as a gap; the fact that they are the same table survives only because the page text was read.

The second finding is a caption collapse. Figures 1 to 5 carry five, four, three, one and four sentences of description; Figures 6 to 11 carry a task number and nothing else - 'Task 2.1', 'Task 2.2', 'Task 3', 'Task 4', 'Task 5', 'Task 6'. The three charts that actually need explaining, the two dual-axis plots and the churn comparison, are the ones captioned with two words.

The third is the excluded region: Figure 1's legend is drawn as a separate bordered box 8 pt below the chart, so the measurer returns it as its own region. It is declared a fragment of Figure 1 and excluded by reason, not deleted.

On the text side, three grids print with no rules at all - Table 2, Table 3 and Table 4 - which is the unruled-grid blind spot this lane keeps meeting. Section attribution needed hand work on seven rows: four sit under a heading printed on the previous page and three sit ABOVE the heading of the section the nearest-heading pass would assign them to, because 3.2, 3.2.1 and 3.3 all print below the pictures on pp6 and 8.
rules: Families: line x3, flowchart-or-schematic x3, bar x2, node-link-network x2, scatter x1, table-grid x1, over twelve rows from thirteen measured regions plus one excluded fragment [geometry.family].

The excluded region is Figure 1's key box on p6, a bordered box of two hatch swatches and their staffing that the Figure 1 caption explicitly describes as a legend substitution. It returns as its own measured region because it is separated from the chart by 8 pt of white, so it is declared excluded rather than counted as a thirteenth exhibit [place.area_frac].

The three chart families are not interchangeable here. Figures 2 and 3 are the only node-link rows - hundreds of nodes in one frame with no axes - while Figures 1, 4 and 11 are schematic diagrams with a handful of labelled boxes on connectors. Figure 11 is the crossover case: it holds six nodes drawn as circles, but it is a two-plane construction diagram with no graph statistics, so it is recorded as a schematic with two panels [geometry.panel_count].

Six captions say nothing. Figures 6 to 11 are captioned 'Task 2.1', 'Task 2.2', 'Task 3', 'Task 4', 'Task 5' and 'Task 6' - a task number with no noun in it. The four figures before them carry two to four descriptive sentences each, so the paper's captioning collapses exactly at the point where the exhibits move from structure diagrams to simulation output [caption.words].

Two of the line rows use a DUAL y axis, and that is the exhibit's argument rather than a styling choice: Figure 7 puts turnover intention on the left and average productivity on the right, and the prose justifies reading the second axis; Figure 8 puts a jagged poisson recruiting cost on one axis against a smooth deterministic training cost on the other. No legend key says which axis belongs to which series, so the colour of the axis title is the only cue [geometry.legend].

Figures 6 and 10 are the same stacked-bar template twice - same three colours, same legend position, same grey panel, same 'Senior Mangers' typo - with the promotion rule the only difference. They are therefore one row each, not one row with two panels, because they print four pages apart and carry different task numbers [geometry.panel_count].

Only Figure 5 has more than one panel among the charts, and its two panels are lettered (a) and (b) inside the picture with their own grey turnover-intention scale bars, on identical axes, and a single arrowed annotation crosses from outside into both [geometry.shared_axes].

THREE PRINTED GRIDS ARE MISSING AND THAT IS DECLARED, NOT PATCHED: Table 2 on p12 (two rows, six level headers across and the service-time requirements under them, no rules at all), Table 3 on p16 (caption at 487.5 pt, four numeric rows to 574.6 pt, no rules) and Table 4 on p17 (caption at 87.1 pt, the same four rows, no rules). All three carry a caption in the text layer and Table 2 is cited three times, so their absence is a measurer result, not a judgement about what they are [place.area_frac].

TABLE 4 REPEATS TABLE 3 NUMBER FOR NUMBER. The sigma sweep on p16 prints 2.314 / 2.083 / 2.250, 0.378 / 0.353 / 0.374, 3.378 / 3.372 / 3.741 and 35.16 / 38.33 / 37.00, and the mu sweep on p17 prints the same twelve values in the same order under a caption that promises a different parameter. The prose reads the second one as an independent confirmation ('comparing the two tests the conclusions are basically the same'), so the paper's second sensitivity result is a copy of its first [caption.verbatim].

Section paths follow the last heading printed above each region, which on four rows is on the previous page: Table 1 under 2.2 on p4, Figure 1 under 3.1.3 on p5, Figure 2 under 3.2.1 on p6, Figure 3 under 3.2.2 on p7. On three more rows the heading for the NEXT section prints below the picture - 3.2 and 3.2.1 on p6 sit at 355.4 and 432.8 pt under a chart that ends at 214.5 pt, and 3.3 on p8 sits at 385.0 pt under a chart that ends at 313.2 pt - so a naive nearest-heading pass files all three in the wrong section [place.section_path].

Citation is complete but thin: eleven of the twelve rows are named in prose and none is never named, yet only Figure 1 is named from a page other than its own or the one before, and no exhibit is named twice. Figures 5 and 6 share a single pointer, 'cf. Figure 5, 6', which is the only place the paper cites two exhibits at once [mention.count].

Area runs from 0.013 for the excluded key box to 0.274 for Figure 2, a factor of twenty-one, and the largest row is the personnel network - the one exhibit whose every point is data rather than layout [place.area_frac].
